about: The Litany of the Most Holy Name of Jesus, which the 1952 Enchiridion Indulgentiarum records under a decree of the Sacred Congregation of Indulgences of 16 January 1886. In that book its two final petitions form one prayer with a single doxology, and this edition retains that Latin recension.

s145.translation: Lord Jesus Christ, who hast said: Ask and ye shall receive; seek and ye shall find; knock and it shall be opened unto you; mercifully grant us, we beseech Thee, the affection of Thy most divine love, that we may love Thee with our whole heart, mouth, and deed, and never cease to praise Thee.

s146.translation: O Lord, grant that we may have a perpetual fear and love of Thy holy Name, for Thou never failest to govern those whom Thou establishest in the steadfastness of Thy love. Who livest and reignest for ever and ever. Amen.

w243.note: The same ambiguity as in the Our Father — malum, evil, or malus, the Evil One. This edition takes malum and marks the doubt.
